scope: Bounded OpenReview/ACL search followed by primary-source reading; not another complete daily crawl or a claim of newly published work today.

work.title: Steering at the Source: Style Modulation Heads for Robust Persona Control
work.metadata_caution: The first-submission date precedes the month encoded in the identifier; preserve the primary page's displayed metadata rather than silently correcting it.
work.formal_publication: ICML 2026, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 306:50230-50271
work.deduplication: One scientific work, linked preprint and proceedings versions; not two independent discoveries.

method_evidence: Methods sections 2-5 locate sparse attention heads geometrically, compare localized versus residual/attention-output interventions, and include zero/random-head ablations. Main models are Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B; GPT-4.1-mini judges trait/coherency. Appendix B.3 uses three humans on selected high-versus-low score pairs. That agreement does not validate subtle real-speaker Japanese differences. Sections7 and appendixF discuss architecture dependence.
prospective_implication: Reliability-preserving style intervention is occupied prior art. A future PersonaSLM algorithm must compare mechanisms and information access, not rename localized steering. No evidence here validates a CPU Q4 2B implementation or the present character-frequency metric. Do not build an intervention solely to improve a weak automatic proxy.
access_failure: Direct OpenReview PDF/forum requests returned a browser challenge. No bypass was attempted; publisher proceedings and arXiv provided the inspected primary evidence. Formal-publication status is supported by PMLR, not inferred from the preprint or a workshop PDF.
monitoring_limit: Existing daily scheduler still collects arXiv/Crossref/OpenAlex metadata. This one manual search does not implement daily OpenReview/ACL/Semantic Scholar collection or scheduled deep review.
